raw_response:
I am thinking like this: my land is only 8.5 mu, so I cannot spread money too loose. I still do what I know best. Wheat and maize are my steady crops, because every year people here do this and it keeps grain coming in. Cotton can make money if the price is all right, but it takes more work. Mungbean does not need too much fertilizer, and if the weather is not too bad it gives me a little extra cash, so I keep some area for it. I did not study much, so I do not count too finely. I look at what happened last year, what my neighbors are doing, and how much cash I can put in without making the family too tight. This year I will not push inputs too hard, but I also will not cut too much, because if wheat or maize turns weak, the loss is bigger than the saved fertilizer money.
